cues.s: Follow one token through a frontier model.
The token is Paris, with its leading space.
It starts in the training data and ends on your screen, crossing twelve stages: how Claude Fable five point two is made, and how it answers you.
Where Anthropic doesn't publish the internals, the drawing uses DeepSeek V4 Pro's design, marked with an asterisk.
Stage one: the corpus.
Web pages, code, books, papers and many languages are pooled into one stream.
Near-duplicates are dropped, classifiers filter out spam and personal data, and the mix is weighted toward code, math and careful prose.
Somewhere in it, a page says the Eiffel Tower is in Paris.
Stage two: tokens.
The model never sees letters.
Byte-pair encoding merges frequent pairs of bytes until common words become single pieces, leading space included.
So Paris is one token, one integer ID.
Images take another road, as patch vectors from a vision encoder.
Stage three: pretraining.
One objective, repeated trillions of times: predict the next token.
Batches flow up the tower in parallel, the loss scores the probability given to Paris, and gradients nudge every weight.
Then the context is stretched toward a million positions.
Stage four: post-training.
Fine-tuning on curated demonstrations teaches the model to follow instructions.
Then it samples a group of attempts, verifiers grade them, and the better-than-average attempts are reinforced.
Written principles add AI feedback, and a penalty keeps the policy close to where it started.
Stage five: release.
The final checkpoint is evaluated for what it can do, and for what it could be misused to do.
Red teams hunt for jailbreaks, safeguards scale with capability, and the results go in a system card.
Safety classifiers ship alongside.
The weights are now frozen.
Stage six: your request.
Months later, you ask for the weather in Paris, with a weather tool attached.
The API is stateless, so every call carries the whole conversation.
Tools, system and messages are rendered in a fixed order, cut by the same tokenizer, and checked against the prompt cache.
Stage seven: the forward pass.
This is the engine, drawn from DeepSeek V4 Pro's published design.
The ID picks one row of the embedding table.
Attention reads earlier positions sparsely.
A router sends the token to six of three hundred and eighty-four experts, plus a shared one.
That repeats sixty-one times, and the head scores the whole vocabulary.
Stage eight: prefill.
Serving runs the frozen tower in two phases.
Prefill pushes every prompt token up at once, in one parallel pass, and each layer caches its keys and values.
Your request shares the hardware with other users, batched continuously.
Stage nine: thinking.
On Fable five point two, thinking is always on.
You set an effort level, from low to max, and the model decides how much to think.
The raw reasoning never leaves the server.
Here, it works out that it can't know today's weather, and should call the tool.
Stage ten: decode.
Now it's a loop: one pass up the tower for each new token, each pass reading the whole cache.
A cheap draft can propose the next token for the big model to verify.
The model writes a tool call: get weather, for the city of Paris.
Stage eleven: streaming.
Token IDs are decoded back into text and streamed to your app as server-sent events, while generation is still running.
The response ends with a stop reason.
Here, the reason is tool use.
Stage twelve: the tool loop.
Claude can't check the weather itself, so your code runs the tool and appends the result.
The whole conversation goes back in, and the unchanged prefix hits the cache.
Decoding resumes, the reply ends, and Paris reaches your screen.
Twelve stages, one token.
Scroll to any stage to read it in detail.
